notes: kb/Work PB548 - THE LAST SENTENCE NOW HOLDS ON EVERY ARM. "A restricted data-pointer shall contain only the predefined address NULL or the address of a data item of the specified type" (cite.py --check 13.18.60.4 -> OK 23)). Its statement-level enforcement is 14.9.39.3 SR19 (both sentences, cite.py --check OK 19)), and SET Format 7 reaches the binder by TWO routes: setAddressStatement -> PtrBinder.BindSetAddress (an ADDRESS OF on either side; already screened) and setToValueStatement / setObjectReferenceStatement -> SetBinder.BindSetPointer (the plain `SET p TO q`), which checked only the category - so `SET P TO R` stored an unrestricted address into a TT-restricted pointer and a based item rebased through it read a PIC X(8) item as type TT (measured before: L=[1234]). Both routes now call ONE screen, PtrBinder.ScreenPointerReceiverRestriction, per receiver: the unrestricted-into-restricted direction (SR19 first sentence) and the converse (SR19's continuation paragraph) are COBOL0869 on the plain spelling too (negatives pb548-*), and the conforming restricted-to-restricted copy and TO NULL run (2002/pb548_set_restricted_pointer_plain: L=[ABCD] / P1-NULL / L2=[ABCD]). The ALLOCATE / CALL-argument / RETURNING arms were already screened (PtrBinder, same StrongTypeModel predicates). Editions narrowed to 2002+ - the TYPE TO phrase and TYPEDEF are 2002 introductions.
